# Synthetic example records

**These files are synthetic.** They are generated by
`dataset/example/build_examples.py` from the repository's own fixtures
(`fixtures/naksa_base.pdf`, `fixtures/naksa_drift.pdf`, `fixtures/photos/`) and
describe no real building and no real person. They exist so the record format,
the consent/withdrawal mechanics and the export pipeline can be reviewed and
tested before any real data is collected.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `karmi-example-0001.json` | full consent (homeowner + drawing author + photographer), CC BY 4.0, 3 photos across stages |
| `karmi-example-0002.json` | CC BY-NC 4.0, one grant covering two roles, scene extracted live from `fixtures/naksa_drift.pdf` |
| `karmi-example-0003.json` | **withdrawn consent** (tier forced to gated); excluded from every export |
| `karmi-example-0003.withdrawal.json` | the redaction instruction produced by `withdraw()` |
| `manifest.json` | machine-readable index: sha256 of each record, scan results, media reports |
| `media/` | EXIF-stripped copies of the fixture photos + their de-identification reports |
| `export/` | output of `python -m dataset.export --example` (JSONL + Hugging Face folder) — regenerated, git-ignored |

Rebuild everything (deterministic — fixed dates, no clock reads in record content):

```bash
python -m dataset build-examples
python -m dataset export --example
```

The builder runs `dataset.deidentify.deidentify_photo` on every fixture photo it
references and `scan_record()` over every finished record; if a record trips a
PII heuristic the build prints it loudly.
